comments.text:
I've been involved in creating multi agent systems myself (extensively), meaning that I actually have experience with creating agent systems like Claude Code. Even if all those things exist, there is still knowledge and context about bigger software dev projects that the multi agent system will not have, and therefore (at the least)  a pull request that a system like that makes will still have to be reviewed.

In other words, at most, this will replace junior developers.


Now if we have a scenario where you could put years of experience with a large scale software project in one prompt, and the LLM wouldnt forget anything in said prompt (which is not the case), then it could potentially be fully automated.

But the bottlenecks are:

- Limited Context Window
- LLMs (even with the newest reasoning models) often times forget the information towards the middle of the prompt. This has gotten a lot better but there is still a threshold where it happens.
- Most software dev projects need years of experience that isnt well documented in written form for LLMs to process

The place where AI is currently failing is with medium to larger size code bases. Programming is a rapidly evolving field with best practices changing every year. That being said I probably only write 5% of the code now and AI writes the rest of it, but it is usually a few prompts of tweaking the code for every new section of code that it creates.
